items.title: Find plant running when the building is empty
items.why: A run status compared with the time schedule and occupancy is a direct check; GenAI only writes the weekly summary.
logic: Every 15 min: equipment on outside its scheduled hours, or with zone and entrance counts at zero (e.g. for 30 min).
Energy wasted = measured kW × time running out of hours.
Weekly: rank by kWh wasted; GenAI drafts a short note per item for the energy manager.
items.output: Out-of-hours events per asset with kWh and cost; weekly summary.
items.example: Sat 14 Nov: AHU-1 ran 06:10–18:40 with the schedule off and 0 people counted; 11.2 kW × 12.5 h = 140 kWh (≈ 21 at 0.15/kWh).

items.title: Weather-corrected monthly energy performance
items.why: A regression of daily energy on cooling degree days and occupancy (IPMVP Option C, ASHRAE Guideline 14). No ML training.
logic: Daily kWh from the main incomer; drop days when the meter was offline.
Cooling degree days from outside air temperature (base e.g. 18 °C, to confirm).
Fit kWh = a + b × CDD + c × people on 12 months; accept only if CV(RMSE) and NMBE meet Guideline 14.
Monthly: actual vs expected, in kWh and %.
items.output: Monthly table and tags: expected kWh, actual kWh, deviation %.
items.example: October: actual 212,400 kWh; expected 198,900 kWh (CDD 402, 1,120 people/day); +6.8%, above the ±5% band.

items.title: Sub-meter reconciliation
items.why: Main minus the sum of sub-meters is arithmetic; drift is a running sum (CUSUM) of that gap.
logic: Daily: unmetered = main − (HVAC + lighting + small power).
Baseline share of unmetered load from the first 60 days.
CUSUM on the daily share; alert when it crosses its limit (e.g. 5 × daily std, to confirm).
items.output: Daily reconciliation tags and drift alerts.
items.example: Unmetered load rose from 6% to 13% over 9 days; CUSUM limit crossed on 19 Nov; likely a failed CT on the small power board.
missing: CT ratios and sub-meter hierarchy (master data)

items.title: Chilled-water temperature reset
items.why: Trim-and-respond on cooling valve positions is a fixed rule; no forecasting needed.
logic: Every 10 min: if the AHU cooling valve is below 85% open and zones are within setpoint, raise the setpoint by 0.3 °C.
If the valve is above 95% or a zone is 1 °C above setpoint, lower by 0.5 °C.
Limits 6.5–10 °C (to confirm). Each change goes to the operator for approval before it is written.
items.output: Setpoint recommendation queue with reason; written to CH1.CHWSTSP after approval.

items.title: Fresh-air reduction on low CO2
items.why: Damper position against a CO2 band is a fixed demand-controlled ventilation rule.
logic: While the fan runs: if return CO2 < 600 ppm and the damper is above minimum, recommend the minimum position (e.g. 20%).
If CO2 > 900 ppm, recommend opening in 10% steps. Operator approves before writing.
items.output: Damper recommendations and hours of excess fresh air per week.
items.example: Tue 10:00–15:00: CO2 480–560 ppm with the damper at 65%; recommend 20%.

items.title: Peak demand warnings
items.why: Projecting the current demand interval against the month's peak is arithmetic.
items.other_inputs: Contracted demand limit; demand interval length (e.g. 30 min).
logic: Every minute: projected interval average = energy so far ÷ elapsed time.
Warn when the projection exceeds the month's peak or 95% of the contracted limit.
items.output: Warning with minutes left in the interval and kW to shed.
items.example: 14:12: projected 1,410 kW against a month peak of 1,380 kW; shed 30 kW within 18 min.

items.title: Maintenance scheduling across the technician team
items.why: Assigning tasks to technicians and days within skills, hours and due dates is an assignment problem; a solver gives the best feasible week.
items.other_inputs: Technician skills, shifts and hours; task durations by type.
logic: Tasks = open work orders plus faults without a work order plus run-hour service intervals due this week.
Variables: task × technician × day. Constraints: skill match, hours per day, one technician per task.
Maximise priority served minus a penalty per day late; solve with CP-SAT (see scripts/optimise/schedule_maintenance.py).
Supervisor approves the plan before work orders are updated.
items.output: Weekly plan per technician and day; unscheduled tasks with the reason.
items.example: Week 48: 23 tasks, 21 scheduled; T2 Monday: chiller fault WO-311 (4 h) then AHU-1 filter (1 h); 2 low-priority tasks moved to next week.
missing: Technician skills and shift rota (CMMS master data)

items.title: Washroom consumables restocking
items.why: Usage per visitor is an average (statistics); the reorder point and order quantity come from a standard inventory model.
items.other_inputs: Supplier lead time, unit cost, order cost.
logic: Daily usage = drop in dispenser level, scaled to people counted.
Refill task when a dispenser is below 20%.
Reorder point = demand over lead time + safety stock (z × σ × √L); order quantity by EOQ (see scripts/optimise/reorder.py).
items.output: Refill tasks for the cleaning team; weekly order list.
items.example: Towels: 41 packs/day average (σ 9), lead time 5 days; reorder at 238 packs, order 610.

items.title: Plain-language questions about the building
items.why: A language model turns the question into read-only queries on the points and explains the result; it never writes.
logic: Map the question to points with the point list and tag descriptions.
Run read-only queries on live values and history.
Answer with the numbers and the point tags used, so every answer can be checked.
items.output: Answers in chat with the tags and time range used.
items.example: Q: Was level 3 warm yesterday afternoon? A: FCU-301 averaged 25.6 °C 14:00–17:00 against 24 °C (FCU301.ZNT); FCU-302 stayed at 24.2 °C.

items.title: Open work orders ranked by urgency
items.why: A weighted score of priority and time left to the SLA, with typical fix times (medians) from closed orders.
logic: Median time to close per priority from the last 6 months.
Score = priority weight × (1 + share of SLA time used); flag orders whose median fix time exceeds the time left.
Re-rank every 30 min.
items.output: Ranked queue with an at-risk flag.
items.example: WO-327 (P2): 70% of SLA used, median fix 6 h, 4 h left → at risk, rank 1.

items.title: Chiller failure prediction weeks ahead
items.reason: Needs a trained failure-prediction model (ML); the policy stops at optimisation.

items.title: Next-day building load forecast
items.reason: Needs a trained forecasting model (ML); the policy stops at optimisation.

items.title: Footfall counting from CCTV video
items.reason: Needs video analytics on the CCTV system; no camera feeds are in the points list.

architecture.does: BMS, meters, people counter, washroom sensors and CMMS, as in the points list.
Historian with quality flags; CMMS integration.
Rules, statistics and optimisation jobs; GenAI for summaries and questions.
Approves setpoint, damper and schedule changes before they are written.
